contexts.text: The man took an ornament of gold () = Divine good... It was customary... to give the bride an ornament of gold and bracelets... and the good of the Church was represented by the ornament... the ornament of gold was placed upon the nose. (Continued. See Nose.) AC 3132.
That a nose-jewel was an ensign of marriage as to good. Illustrated.
A nose-jewel () = an ensign of the good of the Church.
The earrings were of two kinds... those which were applied above the nose to the forehead were ensigns representative of good, and are called nose-jewels.
A ring upon the nose () = the perception of good. AE 272:8.
A ring () = truth as to perception.

The bracelets, chain, nose-jewel, etc. () are insignia by which are signified spiritual things of various kinds... That nose-jewels and earrings are representatives of perception and obedience. References.
A ring upon the nose () = the perception of truth from good.
